content.text: {"persuasion":"PERSUADED","support_scope":"CORE_ONLY","rationale":"The book's core identification — that the single English word 'hell' overlays two distinct biblical referents, Sheol/Hades (the grave that receives righteous and wicked alike) and Gehenna (the final destroying judgment of the wicked) — is carried decisively by the cited texts. Psalm 16:10 places the Messiah's own soul in 'hell' (sheol), which Peter reads at Pentecost as the grave preceding resurrection (Acts 2:27-31); this is unintelligible if 'hell' means the torment-realm of the damned. Matthew 10:28 uses a different word (Gehenna) for a different act (destruction of soul and body), and Jesus keeps the terms apart (gates of hades in Matt 16:18 vs. Gehenna destruction). Revelation 20:13-14, where hades itself is thrown into the lake of fire, makes conflation impossible: the grave cannot be identical to the fire it is cast into. The KJV's own 31/31 split of sheol between 'grave' and 'hell' confirms one word was divided by translators' doctrine. Notably, both common-interpretation surveys concede this lexical distinction is a widely held scholarly position, so the core is not eccentric — it is the best-supported account of the printed texts. What remains contestable is the book's secondary superstructure: full annihilationism, the fire-as-God ontology, and the Plato-to-Augustine genealogy. The strongest counter (traditionalism that grants the Sheol/Gehenna split but holds Gehenna to be eternal conscious punishment) disputes the duration and nature of Gehenna's judgment, not the two-referent core; per the adjudication rules that yields PERSUADED at CORE_ONLY, with the duration dispute logged as unresolved.","book_core_identification":"The English word 'hell' conflates two distinct scriptural referents that must not be equated: Sheol/Hades, the grave/realm of the dead that receives all people including the righteous and the Messiah himself (Ps 16:10; Gen 37:35; Acts 2:27-31), and Gehenna, the final judgment in which God destroys the wicked (Matt 10:28). Doctrine built on the merged English word misidentifies both.","book_secondary_elaborations":["Annihilationism/conditional immortality: the final fate of the wicked is terminal destruction ('second death'), not endless conscious torment","The state of the dead in sheol is unconscious 'sleep' (Eccl 9:5; Ps 6:5; 115:17; 146:4) awaiting resurrection","The unquenchable fire is not a place but God's own presence (Deut 4:24; Heb 12:29), with outcomes determined by 'covering'","'Everlasting punishment' (kolasis/aiōnios) marks permanence of result, not perpetuity of process, on the pattern of Jude 7 and Heb 9:12","Luke 16 (rich man and Lazarus) is a parable about the sufficiency of Moses and the prophets, not afterlife topography","The doctrine of endless torment derives historically from Platonic soul-immortality via Philo, Tertullian, and Augustine","Deuteronomy 28's curse catalogue and the law's proportional, capped, terminal punishments exclude endless torment from God's covenant system","The Cochin manuscript / Targumic 'second death' as final unwaking death"],"strongest_counter_interpretation":"The informed traditionalist reading: grant that Sheol/Hades (intermediate state) and Gehenna (final judgment) are lexically distinct, but hold that both involve conscious experience for the wicked — Hades already contains conscious torment (Luke 16:23-24), and Gehenna is eternal conscious punishment, as shown by the undying worm and unquenchable fire (Mark 9:48), the parallel of 'eternal punishment' with 'eternal life' (Matt 25:46), smoke of torment ascending forever with no rest day or night (Rev 14:11), and the devil, beast, and false prophet 'tormented day and night for ever and ever' in the same lake of fire into which the lost are cast (Rev 20:10, 15). On this reading 'destroy' in Matt 10:28 (apollumi) means ruin or loss, not annihilation.","counter_core_identification":"'Hell' properly denotes the final state of eternal conscious punishment of the unrepentant (Gehenna / lake of fire), with Hades as a conscious intermediate state preceding it; the two stages are distinct but both punitive and conscious for the wicked.","counter_relation_to_book_core":"SAME_CORE_BROADER","material_core_denial":"A material denial of the core would require that 'hell' in Scripture names a single unified torment-realm of the damned, such that Ps 16:10's hell and Matt 10:28's hell are the same place with the same doctrinal content. That denial fails on the supplied evidence: Ps 16:10 puts the Holy One's soul in that 'hell' and Peter preaches it as the grave before resurrection (Acts 2:27-31); Jacob and Job expect to go there (Gen 37:35; Job 14:13); and Rev 20:13-14 casts hades into the lake of fire, formally distinguishing the grave from the final judgment. No reading that merges the two can explain these texts without contradiction.","counter_case":["Luke 16:23-24 depicts a man in hades, conscious and 'tormented in this flame,' suggesting the intermediate state is not silent sleep","Matt 25:46 sets 'everlasting punishment' in grammatical parallel with 'everlasting life,' so equal duration is the natural reading","Mark 9:48's undying worm and unquenched fire imply an unending process, not a completed one","Rev 14:11: 'the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: and they have no rest day nor night' — torment, not smoke alone, is the subject of 'no rest'","Rev 20:10 explicitly says the devil, beast, and false prophet 'shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever' in the same lake of fire that receives the lost (20:15)","Apollumi in Matt 10:28 can denote ruin or loss (as of the 'lost' sheep) rather than cessation of existence","This has been the majority reading of Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant confessions since Augustine"],"book_explanatory_advantages":["Explains why the Messiah, Jacob, Job, and David all go to 'hell'/sheol without being damned — impossible on any unified torment reading (Ps 16:10; Gen 37:35; Job 14:13; Acts 2:27-34)","Explains the KJV's own 31/31 split of one Hebrew word between 'grave' and 'hell' as translator doctrine imposed on a single referent","Explains Rev 20:13-14 mechanically: hades gives up its dead and is itself destroyed in the lake of fire — the grave and the final judgment are two things, one of which ends the other","Explains Jesus' own lexical discipline: gates of hades (Matt 16:18) vs. destruction in Gehenna (Matt 10:28) — never interchanged","Explains the sheol-state texts (Eccl 9:5; Ps 6:5; 115:17; 146:4; Dan 12:2) as unconscious sleep, matching 'the dead in Christ shall rise' and 'David is not ascended'","Explains the total silence of Deut 28's exhaustive curse catalogue on postmortem torment, and coheres with the law's proportional, capped, terminal penal grammar (Exod 21:24; Deut 25:3)","Explains 'destroy both soul and body' (Matt 10:28), 'the soul that sinneth, it shall die' (Ezek 18:4), 'God only hath immortality' (1 Tim 6:16), and the righteous 'seeking' immortality (Rom 2:7) without redefining 'destroy' and 'die'","Explains the eternal-fire idiom by parallel: Jude 7's Sodom suffered 'eternal fire' yet is not burning now; ascending smoke marks completed destruction (Isa 34:10; Rev 19:3; Ps 68:2)","Explains Isa 66:24 precisely: the worm and fire work on 'carcases' viewed by the living, not on conscious sufferers"],"counter_explanatory_advantages":["Reads Rev 20:10's 'tormented day and night for ever and ever' (of devil, beast, false prophet) at face value without appealing to variant manuscripts or genre arguments","Takes the durational parallel of Matt 25:46 in its most immediate grammatical sense","Takes Luke 16's torment imagery as descriptive rather than parabolic furniture","Aligns with the historic majority position of the post-Augustinian church"],"evidence_book_core_cannot_explain":[],"comparative_winner":"BOOK","decisive_sources":["Psalm 16:10 with Acts 2:27-31 (the Holy One's soul in 'hell' = the grave before resurrection)","Matthew 10:28 (a different word, Gehenna, and a different act, destruction of soul and body)","Revelation 20:13-14 (hades delivers up its dead and is itself cast into the lake of fire — grave and final judgment formally distinguished)","Matthew 16:18 vs. Matthew 10:28 (Jesus' consistent separation of hades and Gehenna)","Genesis 37:35; Job 14:13 (righteous men expecting sheol)","The KJV's 31/31 rendering split of sheol between 'grave' and 'hell'","Ecclesiastes 9:5; Psalm 6:5; 115:17; 146:4; Daniel 12:2 (the state of the dead in sheol as unconscious sleep)"],"unresolved_objections":["Revelation 20:10 states the devil, beast, and false prophet are 'tormented day and night for ever and ever' in the lake of fire; the chapter never directly addresses this verse, and it strains the pure-annihilation elaboration even if it concerns non-human figures","Rev 14:11 attaches 'no rest day nor night' to the worshippers of the beast themselves, which the smoke-as-receipt argument does not fully neutralize","The dismissal of Luke 16's imagery as parabolic furniture is defensible but not demonstrated from the supplied texts alone","The appeal to the Cochin Hebrew Revelation and Targumic 'second death' glosses relies on late, non-canonical witnesses of limited evidential weight","The Plato-Philo-Tertullian-Augustine genealogy is a historical claim asserted rather than documented within the supplied evidence","The kolasis-as-pruning etymology is suggestive but etymology alone does not fix first-century usage"],"confidence":"high"}
